title: Crime Reporting System
summary: A full-stack platform where citizens report crimes online, with separate portals for citizens, police and admins.
description: A complete civic-tech platform that lets citizens file crime reports online instead of visiting a police station. The system has three role-based portals — Citizens file and track reports, Police manage and act on cases, and Admins oversee the whole system. Security was the core challenge: the backend is a Spring Boot REST API following SOLID principles, protected with Spring Security, JWT authentication and OTP-based login. Evidence files (photos, documents) are uploaded to AWS S3, and all records live in a normalized MySQL database.
highlights: Role-based access control for three user types (Citizen / Police / Admin)
JWT authentication plus OTP-based login flow
Evidence storage on AWS S3 with secure upload handling
Spring Boot REST API designed around SOLID principles
Modern responsive UI in React.js + Tailwind CSS

title: Money Mentor
summary: A cross-platform desktop app for personal money management, packaged for production with Electron.
description: A desktop money-management application that runs on Windows, macOS and Linux. The UI is built with React.js running inside Electron.js, talking to a Django REST Framework backend with MySQL for secure storage of financial data. The backend was deployed on shared hosting and the desktop app was packaged for production using Electron Builder — a real exercise in shipping software to end users, not just writing it.
highlights: Cross-platform desktop app: one React codebase for all OSes
Django REST Framework backend with MySQL
Production packaging and auto-update setup with Electron Builder
Backend deployed and operated on shared hosting

title: BookBroker
summary: An API-driven e-commerce platform for buying and selling books, with integrated online payments.
description: A fully API-driven e-commerce platform for book selling. The backend is Django REST Framework exposing clean JSON APIs consumed by a React.js + Bootstrap frontend. The Razorpay payment gateway is integrated for secure online transactions, and MySQL manages users, orders and inventory. Deployed on shared hosting — proof that a well-built stack doesn't need expensive infrastructure.
highlights: Razorpay payment gateway integration for real transactions
Fully decoupled architecture: Django REST APIs + React SPA
Order, inventory and user management in MySQL
Deployed and run on budget shared hosting

title: myntome.com
summary: A live online footwear store, independently developed, launched and operated since August 2020.
description: An online footwear e-commerce store launched in August 2020, developed and deployed independently with a friend. This was a real business, not a class project: product catalog, orders, and the full operational side of keeping an online store running. It's where I learned what shipping to real customers actually means — uptime, performance on cheap hosting, and iterating based on user behaviour.
highlights: Launched and operated a real e-commerce business
End-to-end ownership: development, deployment, operations
Built for real customers on a startup budget

title: Covid Tracker
summary: A React dashboard tracking live COVID-19 statistics from the disease.sh public API.
description: A data dashboard built entirely in React.js that visualises live COVID-19 statistics fetched from the public disease.sh API. A compact project that demonstrates working with third-party REST APIs, async data loading states, and presenting live data clearly.
highlights: Live third-party API integration with loading/error states
Clean data presentation in React

title: PizzaBite — Hackathon Project
summary: An online pizza-ordering system built under hackathon time pressure at college.
description: PizzaBite is an online pizza ordering system built in Java during a college hackathon. Working against the clock with a team, we designed and shipped a working ordering flow — a good showcase of building under pressure and dividing work across a team.
highlights: Built and demoed within hackathon time constraints
Team collaboration under deadline pressure
